## Term Review: Talking and Writing About Myself and My Family

- This term, we practiced turning our ideas about **ourselves and our family** into clear sentences — using nouns, verbs, adjectives, and pronouns we've learned.
- **Adjectives** describe people or things (e.g., *beautiful*, *happy*, *big*).
- When **retelling a story**, always start with the beginning, then the middle, then the end — in the correct order.
- A good **summary** shares only the most important parts of a story in a few sentences — not every single detail.
- **Informational texts** give real facts (for example, about families or daily routines), while stories can be made-up.
- Giving a personal **opinion** means saying what you think or feel and explaining why (e.g., "I liked the story because it was funny.")

| Skill | What It Means |
|---|---|
| Retelling | Telling a story again in order: beginning, middle, end |
| Summarizing | Sharing only the most important parts, briefly |
| Opinion | Sharing what you think, with a reason |

- By the end of this term, we should be able to speak and write simple, complete, correctly punctuated sentences about ourselves and our families.

## Comparing Money Values and Solving Money Word Problems

- To **compare** two amounts of money, ask which one is bigger. We use these signs: **>** (greater than), **<** (less than), and **=** (equal to).
- Example: ₱200 **>** ₱150, because 200 is more than 150.
- To arrange amounts from **least to greatest**, list the smallest amount first and the biggest amount last.
- **Word problems** with money usually ask us to add two or more amounts together. Steps to solve:
  1. Find the amounts mentioned in the problem.
  2. Decide if you need to **add** them together.
  3. Add carefully, then write your answer with the ₱ sign.

| Problem | Amounts | Total |
|---|---|---|
| Toy + Book | ₱150 + ₱80 | ₱230 |
| Snacks + Notebook | ₱100 + ₱50 | ₱150 |

- Some problems have **two steps** — you may need to add money received more than once before you get the final total. Read slowly and add one step at a time.

quiz.correct_answer: ₱5 coin

## Term Review: Living Things and Caring for Our Senses

- **Living things** breathe, eat, grow, move on their own, and respond to their surroundings — examples: people, animals, and plants.
- **Nonliving things** do not do these things — examples: rocks, toys, and furniture.
- Some things, like a dried leaf or a piece of wood, were **once part of a living thing** but are no longer growing.
- All living things share **basic needs**: air, food or nutrients, water, space, and shelter.
- Our **five sense organs** — eyes (sight), ears (hearing), nose (smell), tongue (taste), and skin (touch) — help us learn about the world, and we often use more than one sense at the same time (like tasting and smelling food together).
- Caring for our senses means washing hands and face, reading with good lighting, protecting our ears from loud sounds, and telling an adult if something hurts.

| Category | Examples |
|---|---|
| Living things | Dog, plant, ant, person |
| Nonliving things | Rock, chair, pencil, toy car |
| Sense organs | Eyes, ears, nose, tongue, skin |

- A good scientist always **observes carefully first** before deciding whether something is living or nonliving — this is an important investigation skill!

## Balik-Aral: Pagsasalita at Pagsusulat Tungkol sa Sarili at Pamilya

- Ngayong termino, natutunan nating baguhin ang ating mga ideya tungkol sa **ating sarili at pamilya** tungo sa malinaw na pangungusap — gamit ang pangngalan, pandiwa, pang-uri, at panghalip na natutuhan.
- Ang **pang-uri** ay naglalarawan ng tao o bagay (hal. *maganda*, *masaya*, *malaki*).
- Kapag **muling isinasalaysay** ang isang kuwento, laging simulan sa simula, pagkatapos ang gitna, at panghuli ang wakas — ayon sa tamang pagkakasunod-sunod.
- Ang mabuting **buod** ay naglalaman lamang ng pinakamahalagang bahagi ng kuwento sa iilang pangungusap — hindi lahat ng detalye.
- Ang pagbibigay ng **opinyon** ay nangangahulugang sinasabi mo kung ano ang iniisip o nararamdaman mo, kasama ang dahilan (hal. "Nagustuhan ko ang kuwento dahil nakakatawa ito.")

| Kasanayan | Kahulugan |
|---|---|
| Muling pagsasalaysay | Pagsasabi ulit ng kuwento ayon sa tamang pagkakasunod-sunod |
| Pagbubuod | Pagsasabi lamang ng pinakamahalagang bahagi, nang maikli |
| Opinyon | Pagsasabi ng iniisip mo, may dahilan |

- Sa pagtatapos ng termino, dapat kaya na nating magsalita at magsulat ng payak, wasto, at magalang na pangungusap tungkol sa ating sarili at pamilya.

## Term Review: Computer Parts, Safe Use, and Mouse Skills

- **Computer parts** we have learned: the **monitor** (shows pictures and words), the **CPU/system unit** (the "brain" of the computer), the **keyboard** (for typing), and the **mouse** (for pointing and clicking).
- To turn on a computer **safely**, press the power button and wait for it to start up properly.
- To turn it off, always **shut it down properly** first — never unplug it right away, since this can damage the computer or cause us to lose our work.
- **Mouse skills** we practiced this term: **single-click** (select), **double-click** (open quickly), **click-and-drag** (move something), and **scroll** (see more of a page).
- Taking care of our equipment matters too: clean, dry hands, no food or drinks near the computer, and asking an adult for help with plugs and wires.

| Skill/Part | What to Remember |
|---|---|
| Monitor | Shows pictures and words |
| CPU | The computer's "brain" |
| Start-up/Shutdown | Always shut down properly, don't just unplug |
| Mouse Skills | Click, double-click, drag, scroll |

- By the end of this term, we should be able to confidently name computer parts, start up and shut down safely, and use the mouse with control.

## Balik-Aral: Ang Komunidad at ang Magkakaugnay na Tungkulin ng Bawat Miyembro

- Ang **komunidad** ay isang grupo ng tao na magkakasama sa iisang lugar (tulad ng barangay) na may magkakatulad na pangangailangan at gawain.
- Ang bawat komunidad ay may sariling **heograpikong anyo** (ilog, bundok, dagat) at mga **institusyon** (paaralan, ospital, palengke) na tumutugon sa magkakaibang pangangailangan ng mga tao.
- Sinasabing **magkakaugnay (interdependent)** ang mga miyembro ng komunidad — nakadepende sila sa isa't isa. Halimbawa: nagtatanim ang magsasaka ng gulay na ibinebenta ng tindera sa palengke.
- Kahit maliit ang tila ginagawa ng isang miyembro, mahalaga pa rin ito para sa ikabubuti ng lahat.
- Bilang bata, makatutulong tayo sa ating komunidad sa pamamagitan ng pagsunod sa mga tuntunin at paggalang sa kapwa.

| Miyembro | Kontribusyon |
|---|---|
| Magsasaka | Nagtatanim ng pagkain |
| Tindera | Nagbebenta ng mga produkto sa palengke |
| Bata | Sumusunod sa tuntunin, gumagalang sa iba |

- Ang pangunahing aral: dapat nating kilalanin, igalang, at pahalagahan ang bawat miyembro ng ating komunidad, dahil magkakaugnay ang kanilang mga tungkulin para sa ikabubuti ng lahat.

## Ang 3Rs: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle

- Ang **3Rs** ay tatlong paraan upang maalagaan ang kalikasan at mabawasan ang basura: **Reduce** (pagbawas), **Reuse** (muling paggamit), at **Recycle** (muling pagproseso).
- **Reduce** — pagbawas sa dami ng ginagamit o binibili, tulad ng pagdadala ng sariling bag sa halip na kumuha ng maraming plastik.
- **Reuse** — paggamit muli ng isang bagay sa halip na itapon agad, tulad ng paggawa ng lapisan mula sa lumang lata.
- **Recycle** — paggawa ng bagong bagay mula sa lumang materyales, tulad ng paggawa ng bagong papel mula sa lumang papel.
- Mahalaga ring ihiwalay ang **nabubulok (biodegradable)** na basura sa **di-nabubulok** upang mas madali itong maproseso.

| R | Kahulugan | Halimbawa |
|---|---|---|
| Reduce | Pagbawas | Magdala ng sariling bag |
| Reuse | Muling paggamit | Gawing lalagyan ang lumang bote |
| Recycle | Muling pagproseso | Gumawa ng bagong papel mula sa luma |
